paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. The horizontal axis represents nine language families—IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic—ordered from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. For each language family, six model configurations are represented by grouped bars: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light pink), and XLM-B2 (dark red), as indicated by the legend. In IE-Indic, the tallest bars are for mBERT-R2 and mBERT-B2, both reaching approximately 20–25, while other configurations are lower. IE-Germanic shows consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all models, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) are significantly taller than the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, and the mBERT-L2 bars in this group reach approximately 15. The Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. The bars are not sorted and are presented in the order of the language families as listed on the horizontal axis.
